name: Docker
abstract: Conformance class for OGC API - Processes Part 2 (DRAFT). Defines requirements for Docker-based execution units in OGC Application Packages.

sources.title: OGC API - Processes - Part 2: Deploy, Replace, Undeploy

description:
# Overview This clause defines the requirements for describing, in the execution unit of an [OGC Application Package](#sec-7), a processes’ executable code encapsulated in a Docker container. # Schema # Properties type and image # Property deployment # Property config # Property bindings ## Overview
**NOTE:** If a binding information is not specified, it is assumed that the processing server will apply some internally-defined default mapping; this is an implementation detail and beyond the scope of this Standard.
## Input binding ### Overview The following input binding parameters can be specified: - **prefix**: - A prefix to be added before an argument value that is used for the execution unit invocation. - **position**: - The value can be an integer or a string. - If it is an integer then it is assumed to be 0-based and the argument is added in this position to the execution unit invocation. - If the value is a string then it should be an expression that evaluates to single integer value or null. - If the value expression evaluates to null, nothing is added to the execution unit invocation. - **valueFrom**: - If the `valueFrom` is a constant string value then this value is added verbatim as an argument to the execution unit invocation. - If the `valueFrom` is an expression, evaluate the expression to yield the actual value and add that as an argument to the execute unit invocation. - If the `valueFrom` is null, nothing is added to the execution unit invocation. - **itemSeparator** - Join the array elements into a single string with the elements separated by the `itemSeparator` and add that as an argument to the execution unit invocation. - **shellQuote** - A boolean that controls whether the value used as an argument in the execution unit invocation is quoted or not. - A value of `true` (the default value) means metacharacters or directives are not interpreted when the execution unit is invoked. - If metacharacters or directives need to be specified when the execution unit is invoked the value of this parameter should be set to `false`. ### Macro substitution in expressions The value of a binding parameters can be an expression. The macro syntax “$(…​)” can be used to reference an process input value in an expression. - The value `self` (e.g. `$(self)`) refers to the value of the current process input in the current execution unit invocation. - The value `inputs.` (e.g. `$(inputs.arg2)`) refers to the value of another process input in the current execution unit invocation. - If the input is defined as a string type of format “file” or “directory”, the following meta-values can be used to manipulate the file or directory path without having to resort to complex regular expressions. - “.path” returns the path of a name without the basename - “.basename” returns the name of the file or directory without the path - “.nameroot” returns the basename with any extension - “.nameext” return the extension of the basename ## Output binding The optional `glob` parameter can be used in an output binding to define a wildcard pattern to find the output on a disk or a mounted volume. The same [macro expressions](#sec-8.6.2.2) that can be used in an input binding expression can also be used with `glob` expressions.
